summary: Retain continuation ownership evidence, reject continuations with no remaining useful effect, and remove unused compiler publication work on older engines.
details: Dedicated stream conflicts reach the combined ownership resolver, preserving the winning effect, the continuation's unique effects, and the conflict and omission ledger.
Native-owner coverage that removes every continuation effect creates a rejected candidate instead of a paid zero-effect technology.

The off weapon-overlap setting preserves exact positive generic/dedicated gun-speed pairs with an auditable retained-overlap disposition; arbitrary and same-operation duplicates still fail validation.
Engines without mod-data retain one budget-checked compiler evidence log and avoid constructing public artifacts they cannot emit.
A bounded cache reuses digests only for exact immutable canonical strings; mutable inputs are still serialized and validated, and MIR32 digest identity is unchanged.
Controlled characterization and static checks cover these changes; final engine, performance and release qualification remain required. No measured performance improvement is claimed here.
